questions.q_en:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent sentence.

A. Consumption of food prepared

B. An important food-related

C. Is the increase in

D. Lifestyle change of the past two decades

E. Away from home
questions.solution_en:
The correct order to form a meaningful and coherent sentence is BDCAE. Part B comes first as it sets the context that the sentence will discuss something related to food. Part D follows logically because it specifies what kind of change or trend related to food is being discussed. It introduces the main topic of the sentence, which is the change in lifestyle over the past two decades (Accordingly, BD forms a logical pair). Part C logically follows D because it continues the thought about the lifestyle change introduced in D. It suggests that there has been an increase in something related to this change. Part A then specifies what has increased (consumption of food) as mentioned in C. It talks about the consumption of food that is prepared in a certain manner or location. Part E concludes the sentence by specifying where the food is prepared (away from home). Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

The complete sentence is: An important food-related lifestyle change of the past two decades is the increase in consumption of food prepared away from home.

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has an error in its tense. Identify the error and select the correct sentence from the given options.

I will be arrange all the necessary materials for the programme.
options_en: I is arrange all the necessary materials for the programme.
I was arrange all the necessary materials for the programme.
I would arranging all the necessary materials for the programme.
I will be arranging all the necessary materials for the programme.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence uses "will be arrange," which is incorrect. The future continuous tense requires "will be" followed by the gerund form (verb + -ing), so it should be "will be arranging."

I is arrange...: Incorrect subject-verb agreement ("I" requires "am") and wrong tense ("is arrange" is not a valid form). Negated as it contains multiple errors.

I was arrange...: Incorrect because "was arrange" is not a valid verb form; it should be "was arranging" for past continuous. Also, the sentence requires future tense. Negated as it does not fit the context.

I would arranging...: Incorrect because "would" is followed by the base verb for conditional (e.g., "would arrange") or "be arranging" for conditional continuous. Negated as it is grammatically incorrect.

I will be arranging...: Correctly uses the future continuous tense ("will be arranging") to indicate an ongoing action in the future.

Corrected Sentence: I will be arranging all the necessary materials for the programme.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The girl told her mother that she had finished her homework.
options_en: The girl said to her mother, "I have finished my homework."
The girl said to her mother, "I have to finish my homework."
The girl said to her mother, "I will finish my homework."
The girl said to her mother, "She has to finish my homework."
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Present Perfect Tense.

Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 +Object) will be converted into Present Perfect (Subject + has/have + V3 +Object).

For example:

He said that he had got a new job. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I have got a new job." (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:
Indirect SpeechDirect Speech
toldSaid to
She, herI, my
had finishedhave finished

From the given options, the sentence that follows the above mentioned conditions for Direct speech is option (a) "The girl said to her mother, "I have finished my homework.""

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

NOTE:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

questions.q_en:
Which of the following words has a similar meaning to the underlined word?

It is unwise to openly disparage your colleagues' efforts if you want a cooperative work environment.
questions.solution_en:
Disparage - refers to representing something or someone as being of little worth; to belittle.

a) Discourage - This means to cause someone to lose confidence or enthusiasm. While disparaging someone can be discouraging, it is not the same action.

b) Compare - This means to estimate, measure, or note the similarity or dissimilarity between things. It is unrelated.

c) Belittle - This means to make someone or something seem unimportant. This is a direct and accurate synonym for "disparage."

d) Analyse - This means to examine something methodically and in detail. This is unrelated to belittling.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. This profound philosophy treats breakage and repair as an integral part of the history of an object, rather than as something to be shamefully disguised.

B. Kintsugi is the exquisite Japanese art of repairing broken pottery by mending the areas of breakage with lacquer dusted or mixed with powdered gold or silver.

C. Consequently, the repaired ceramic piece is often considered more beautiful and valuable than the original, as it proudly showcases its scars as a mark of resilience.

D. Instead of attempting to hide the cracks, this unique method deliberately highlights them, celebrating imperfection as a beautiful part of the object's unique journey through time.
questions.solution_en:
The correct sequence is BADC. Sentence B serves as the ideal introduction by defining the subject, "Kintsugi," and explaining the basic technique. Sentence A builds upon this by explaining the "profound philosophy" behind the art form mentioned in B. Sentence D elaborates on "this unique method" by contrasting it with typical repair, emphasizing how it "deliberately highlights" the cracks, which directly follows the philosophical point in A. Sentence C, with its transition word "Consequently," provides the logical conclusion, explaining the result of this artistic and philosophical approach, that the repaired piece becomes more beautiful.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
Directions [Set of 5 Questions]: Directions: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The population of Venice, more than 170,000 after the second world war, has ____________(A) steadily to some 52,000 today. Remaining residents still feel _______________(B) to live in a city of such beauty, many believing their culture survives despite the onslaught, but they also grieve at the losses, lose heart, and move away at a rate of 1,000 a year to homes on the mainland. A Venice without Venetians - without significant numbers of permanent residents - is ______________(C) for as early as 2030. It is no ________________(D) to say that mass tourism - adding to Venice's existing issues with mismanagement of the environment, corruption, political stasis and now the climate emergency - is bringing the community, the lagoon, and a fabulous heritage to within a ___________(E) of collapse.

Which of the following can fit in the blank A?
questions.solution_en:
The given blank will take the word 'dropped' as the auxiliary verb 'has' is followed by a past participle. Also, the given sentence talks about decrease in population of Venice today. 'Concurrently' which is an adverb can be eliminated. 'Risen' (means 'moved from a lower position to a higher one; come or go up') and 'censured' (means 'expressed severe disapproval of (someone or something)' do not fit contextually in the given blank. Hence, the answer is option c).

Note: Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

Auxiliary verb: A verb that gives grammatical information that is not given by the main verb of a sentence. It supports the main verb. Auxiliary verbs help to form the various tenses, moods, and voices of other verbs. The principal ones are be, do, and have. Example: She will sing a song tomorrow. Here, 'will' is the auxiliary verb that supports the main verb 'sing'.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

Rajeev said, "I met my old friend from high school when I tried to catch a bus."
options_en: Rajeev says that he met his old friend from high school when he was trying to catch a bus.
Rajeev said that he has met his old friend from high school when he tried to catch a bus.
Rajeev said that he had met his old friend from high school when he had been trying to catch a bus.
Rajeev said that he met his old friend from high school when he tried to catch a bus.
questions.solution_en:
If the sentence is in Simple Past, the form of tense doesn't change when it is used in the time clause.

One way of identifying the time clause is that the Time clause always begins with the following: When, whenever, while, as, since, after, before, until, as soon as

For example:

Ayush said to me, "When I saw him, he was working." (Direct Speech)

Ayush told me that when he saw him, he was working. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· The pronoun 'I' is changed into 'he' and the possessive determiner 'my' is changed into 'his'.

· Inverted commas ("...") are replaced with 'that'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (d): Rajeev said that he met his old friend from high school when he tried to catch a bus.

questions.q_en:
Select the grammatically correct statement from among the given options.

A. The photo captured an beautiful sunset. It was captured during an our vacation in the Maldives.

B. A photo captured an beautiful sunset. It was captured during our vacation in the Maldives.

C. An photo captured the beautiful sunset. It was captured during our vacation in a Maldives.

D. The photo captured a beautiful sunset. It was captured during our vacation in the Maldives.
questions.solution_en:
The definite article 'the' should be used before 'photo' and 'Maldives' because in both instances, it introduces specific nouns, that is, 'a particular photo that captured a sunset' and 'a place (Maldives)'.

The indefinite article 'a' should be used before 'beautiful' as it is referring to an unspecified noun, that is, 'sunset'. Since 'beautiful' is not a vowel-sounding word, 'an' cannot be used before it.

The sentences A, B, and C depict grammatically incorrect usage of the articles.

Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

Note:

Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

As our digital footprints grow larger, the concept of a digital afterlife is becoming more relevant and more complex. Every photo, post, message, and online interaction we leave behind contributes to an enduring virtual identity that can outlive our physical selves. Companies are now offering services to preserve or even simulate one's personality through AI-powered chatbots and memorial pages. These digital replicas can comfort grieving families or serve as a time capsule for future generations. However, the ethics surrounding data immortality raise tough questions: who controls your data after death? Can a digital persona truly represent the emotional depth of a human being? Some argue this trend devalues death's finality, while others see it as a new form of legacy. As laws scramble to catch up with technology, society must grapple with whether the right to be remembered also includes the right to digitally disappear. The digital afterlife is no longer science fiction - it's quietly becoming our reality.

Option (c) "Preserves" means to keep safe or maintain, which does not match the meaning of "devalues".

Option (d) "Celebrates" means to honour or praise, which is also the opposite of "devalues".

questions.q_en: Select the option with the correct use of future tense.
options_en: I hope your health is getting better by next week.
I hope your health will get better by next week.
I hope your health have been getting better by next week.
I hope your health is get better by next week.
questions.solution_en:
We need the correct future tense for a prediction tied to "by next week":

· Option 1: "I hope your health is getting better by next week" uses present continuous, implying an ongoing action now, not a future state, which mismatches "by next week."

· Option 2: "I hope your health will get better by next week" uses "will" (simple future), correctly indicating a future improvement by a specific time.

· Option 3: "I hope your health have been getting better by next week" uses "have been getting" (present perfect continuous), which is plural and incorrect for singular "health," and the tense doesn't align with a future point.

· Option 4: "I hope your health is get better by next week" is ungrammatical ("is get" is incorrect; it should be "is getting" or "will get").

Option 2 properly uses the future tense, making it the answer.

Arnab says, "I want to be the best English teacher in India." (Direct Speech)

Arnab says that he wants to be the best English teacher in India. (Indirect Speech)

Subham will say, "Kaustav is always late." (Direct Speech)

Subham will say that Kaustav is always late. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

 Inverted commas are removed and 'that' is added after the reporting verb 'says'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: His friend says that he is still staring at the building as we speak.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

Our marketing endeavours focus on building a deep emotional connection since creating an appreciation for platinum's unique qualities.

questions.solution_en:
The correct answer is option (d) as it maintains a clear and coherent structure in expressing the focus of marketing endeavours.

Let us look at the incorrect options:

Option (a): The preposition "in" is incorrect; it should be "focus on building." Therefore, this option has a preposition error.

Option (b): There is a subject-verb agreement error in this option. The plural subject "Our marketing endeavours" should take the plural verb "focus," not the singular verb "focuses."

Option (c): The use of "since" is not suitable in this context. "Since" is used to express a cause or reason, but it doesn't appropriately connect the ideas in the sentence. Any conjunction like "while" is more fitting for expressing simultaneous actions.

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below. While the first and the last sentences (1 and 6) are in the correct order, the sentences in between are jumbled up. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

1) There are some backward areas in Andhra Pradesh.

A. Rayalaseema is one of them.

B. Massive degradation of natural resources and extensive changes in land use have resulted in good productivity in Rayalaseem1.

C. The National Soil Survey and Land use planning organisation is doing its job by giving suggestions to the farmers of Rayalaseem1.

D. Soil Organic Carbon (SOC), which is crucial for maintaining soil quality, has decreased by 84% in the region. Poor soil fertility and soil degradation, like in Rayalaseema region, are the major causes of food shortage.

6) The advice is about which crops are to be cultivated and which not.
questions.solution_en:
After reading the sentences, it can be noted that the central theme of the passage is the condition of soil fertility in Andhra Pradesh. Sentence A forms a mandatory pair with sentence 1, as the latter talks about backward areas in Andhra Pradesh, indicating that Rayalaseema is one of them (through sentence A). Sentence A is followed by sentence B which talks about the exact condition of Rayalaseema in terms of its natural resources. Sentence D continues with the information provided in sentence B and explains the effect of poor soil fertility in Rayalaseema. Sentence C follows D, in which the role of the National Soil Survey and Land use planning are mentioned in countering the coil fertility issue in Rayalaseema and sentence 6 concludes the passage. Therefore, the correct order is 1ABDC6.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in the future tense form.

It took some time to adapt to the new software interface.
options_en: It had taken some time to adapt to the new software interface.
It has taken some time to adapt to the new software interface.
It takes some time to adapt to the new software interface.
It will take some time to adapt to the new software interface.
questions.solution_en: To express a sentence in the future tense, we typically use the modal auxiliary verb "will", followed by the base form of the main verb. Now, to convert this sentence to the future tense, we need to change the verb "took" to its future tense form. The future tense of "took" is "will take." Option (d) correctly uses the future tense ("will take") to express the idea of the original sentence. Therefore, option (d) is the correct answer.
